utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Good morning to everybody. Could we please hear the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning. This is Case Number IT-97-24-T, the Prosecutor versus Milomir Stakic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. And the appearances, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Nicholas Koumjian with Ruth Karper for the Office of the Prosecutor. Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Branko Lukic, John Ostojic, and Danilo Cirkovic for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. Before we ask the usher to bring in our witness of today, can you give us an estimate of the length of time you would need for the cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. We can. Approximately we believe it would take an hour to an hour and a half.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Okay. This will be extremely good, possibly then we can restrict our session of today to one and a half hour if it's agreeable for the parties.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: It's agreeable.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. Then may the usher please bring in the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness X.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: We will hear now the questions of the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: [Witness answered through interpreter].

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness X. My name is John Ostojic, and along with Branko Lukic and Danilo Cirkovic we represent Dr. Stakic. I'm going to ask you a series of questions here today. As the Court has previously indicated to other witnesses, sir, you are still under oath. If at any time you don't understand my question, can you please let me know and I'll try to rephrase it for you. And you have to keep all your answers verbal or oral, and not use shrugs of the shoulders or nods of the head. Fair enough?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Fair enough.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Sir, I had an opportunity to review three statements that were provided to us by the OTP. Initially, from those statements, it seems that you had given several additional statements to various entities. Can you list for us the statements and/or interviews that you gave in connection with your detention at Trnopolje camp as well as that which you witnessed at Mount Vlasic in August of 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: All the statements I gave, I think, come down to the same thing, but in the statements, different questions were asked. However, if you read the three statements, I think they all boil down to more or less the same essence, the same point.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: My question specifically, Mr. Witness X, is whether or not you gave additional statements to any entities other than the three statements that were presented to us by the OTP.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think part of the witness's answer may require a closed session

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Closed session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: We have visitors in the box today.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Private session actually. I didn't use the correct word. They can remain, but it will be silent.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Okay. Sorry, let's change to private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Confirmed.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Witness X, we are now in open session. We covered some of the statements that you had provided to the individual entities reflecting your experiences at Trnopolje camp and Mount Vlasic, specifically I'd like to ask you about the September 1992 ICRC statement. Do you recall that statement, sir, at all?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. But not that clearly, not so clearly as to be able to tell you exactly -- to repeat exactly what I said, what I said to those people. In those moments when the guards prepared us in the room where we were sleeping, the aim of that preparation was to conceal the truth, to keep me from telling the truth for my own safety.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Is it your testimony, sir, that the statement you gave to the ICRC was not truthful or had some misstatements within that statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: The statement was completely untruthful.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Unfortunately, sir, I don't have the benefit of having that statement with me at this time, but is it within that statement that you identified yourself as being also a part of the Muslim resistance in the Brdo region in 1992, and in fact you told them that you were wounded while fighting against Serbs in that area. True or false?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Does the OTP have a copy of this document? We would appreciate also to have one copy of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: We join in the Court's request. We don't have one as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Can the usher be asked to provide a copy before proceeding.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, it was disclosed to the Defence on the 18th of June -- of January, excuse me, of this year. I only have with me one copy of the English translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I don't know by whom a copy would be produced, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: [redacted]. It's four years ago. If it's noted down there that you announced that you want to send it, did you really send it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Okay. The Defence may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Just to clarify, I think I gave the Court what I thought was the UNHCR statement. It's actually the statement given to the Banja Luka state security. I have to look and see if I have that UNHCR.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Just so the record is clear, Your Honour, the UNHCR statement is not what we're dealing with. It's the ICRC statement that we're dealing with. It's referenced specifically just so we're all clear on the May 19th, 1998 statement which is where we derived some of the information, specifically on ERN number 03004395 under the third full-paragraph answer where purportedly the witness states, I'll quote the last sentence in there: "In addition, I gave details to the International Red Cross at this time; however, I did not tell the truth here out of fear." We were questioning on that specifically, although we would appreciate from the OTP that they provide us both the ICRC as well as the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. UNHCR statements if in their possession. And just so the record is clear, we did not receive according to our records receive the September 1992 ICRC statement as suggested in January of 2002 or have no record of it in any event.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: To correct myself, the document that was photocopied is the statement given to the Banja Luka police, and that's what was disclosed in January of 2002. I read it too quickly. It was a September 1992 statement, but it was a different source. It was to the police in Banja Luka. As for an ICRC or UNHCR interview, our computer check that I have in front of me now indicates that we do not have either of those interviews.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If I may proceed, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Witness X, respectfully, you state that the entire statement given to the ICRC was false. Can you tell us why you gave them a false statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: I gave a false statement because I was forced to give a false statement. I was not in a position to give a truthful statement because of the guards watching over us at Paprikovac in Banja Luka. We were ordered not to give a truthful statement, but just to make up a story in any way we could. And that's exactly what I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Share with us, Mr. Witness X, what story did you give the ICRC?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told the ICRC that as a civilian, I lost my leg, that I was hit by a shell and that a shrapnel hit my leg, and that was how I lost my leg. And what you've mentioned already about being a member of a paramilitary unit or army, that's not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If I may turn to another subject, Mr. Witness X, in connection with the police academy in Sarajevo, can you give me the specific name of that entity in 1991 and 1992 in which you attended?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: How do you mean "entity"? Can you clarify that, please. Do you mean the name of the school? It was the police school at Vrace. That's what it was called.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And that was a four-year programme. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And do you know how long that police school at Vrace was in existence prior to 1991 or 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: It existed before the war. It was a regular police school or academy.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you this: With respect to the disbanding of the school, is it true, sir, that it disbanded on April 6th, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't give you the exact date. I don't remember whether it was the 5th or the 6th of April. That's when it was disbanded. But I can't remember because events are starting to fade from my memory. I think it was the 5th or the 6th.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: That's close enough. We'll accept the 5th or the 6th for our purposes. It's not necessarily that relevant. But in any event it was about the time of the outbreak of the war; namely, the secession and separation and independence of Bosnia from the former Yugoslavia. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was when Bosnia was recognised as an independent state by the United Nations.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, following that disbanding of the police academy or the police school that you attended, you returned to Prijedor in April of 1992. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And in fact, sir, did you not also register with the local police to become a police cadet or a reservist?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were told to report because the school had been disbanded, so we were told to report to the nearest local police station to tell them that the school had been disbanded and we all did that. And then I went home.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: So you registered actually with the Muslim police chief Fikret Kadiric, correct, in Prijedor in 1992? Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. He was the chief of the police station at the time. Regardless of ethnicity, regardless of his nationality, he was the chief of police, and he was the person we were supposed to report to.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I'm just reading from your statement, sir, given on the 19th of May, 1998. ERN number 03004392, first full paragraph, third line. The document is not paginated, Your Honour. The ERN number is 03004392.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Page 3 in my collection.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: The first full paragraph -- yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Yes, page 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Page 3 of that document, the first full paragraph starting with the word: "On 6 April, 1992..." --

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: May I proceed, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: It states: "Hasan Balic our academy principal ordered the academy be disbanded. He advised the police cadets to find their own way to safety. I went back to Prijedor and registered as a police cadet with the Muslim police chief Fikret Kadiric." There's another sentence. I'll read that as well. "However I was not assigned to duties and so went to my parents' home and spent the next few months there." My question to you, sir, is it true that when you returned to Prijedor, that you registered as a police cadet with the Muslim police chief Fikret Kadiric?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's correct that I did register and that I went home. That's what we were ordered to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Fair enough.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that point in time, I had no idea that the war would break out. I was planning to go back to that academy.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, help me with this: This is after you left the academy. You in fact, in your statement state that war had already broken out and that's why the school was disbanded, and that's why you returned back to your home in Biscani. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No audible response]

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: So war broke out already. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it had broken out, that's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Is it your testimony, sir, that this Fikret Kadiric was actually the police chief or was he the chief of transportation for the police in April 1992, or do you not recall?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think he was the chief of police.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: From April 6th or thereabouts after the outbreak of war and your departure from Sarajevo upon coming back home to Biscani in April of 1992, can you tell me, sir, at any time from April until April 30th, 1992, whether the population as a whole was asked to turn in their weapons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, when Hambarine was taken, when the incident at Hambarine happened, then the population was asked to return weapons, to hand in weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Just so we have it clear, sir, so from the takeover, April 30th, 1992, until May 22nd, 1992, which is the date that we've generally accepted, I believe, as the incident at Hambarine, is it your testimony that at no time did any authorities ask or seek that the members of the population at large turn in their weapons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Help me reconcile this: On page 5 -- strike that. On page 4 of your 19th May, 1998, statement which has the ERN number 03004394, I believe it's the second paragraph in the answer midway into the answer, sir, it states here and I'll quote: "I believe it was in April 1992 that there was a meeting of the Muslim population in our village of Biscani. Here we were told that the Serbs had demanded written statements of loyalty from the Muslim policemen. They would also in the future have to wear Serbian insignia on their uniforms. If this demand were not met, the Serbs would take action as in Vukovar and would kill recalcitrant Muslims. But we Muslims and especially the Muslim policemen did not heed these demands which were also put forward in other Muslim villages." My question to you, sir, just for clarification first, did this happen before or after the incident in Hambarine?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it happened before the incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me, sir, what you meant when you said "but we Muslims, and especially the Muslim policemen did not heed these demands which were also put forward in other Muslims villages"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we didn't want to wear Serbian insignia. We didn't want to work wearing such insignia. We were opposed to this, and we all agreed that we would not sign an oath of loyalty and wear Serbian insignia on our uniforms and work wearing such insignia.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: This April 1992 meeting that you mentioned with the Muslim population in your village, can you tell me how many people were present?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me, sir, how many such meetings you attended in April of 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only one meeting of that type.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Did this request to wear the Serbian insignia occur, sir, before or after the takeover of the Prijedor Police Station on or about April 30th or May 1st, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: The police station was forcibly taken in the night leading up to the 1st of May. I can't remember exactly whether this happened before or after that. I'm not trying to conceal anything, I simply can't say because it's faded from my memory.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I understand that, sir, and respect it. And I'm just trying to get clarification on this. On that same page 4 of your 19th May, 1998, document ERN number 03004394, which we were just referencing, you state on the last sentence of that document --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Sorry, it's page 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: On page 5 of that statement you state, again second paragraph last sentence: "In what I believe was a response to this - meaning the request for the Serb insignia - the Serbs took over the police station on 1 May 1992." Does this, sir, help refresh your recollection as to whether or not the request from the Serbs who purportedly demanded written statements of loyalty and also requested Serbian insignia be worn on the Muslim police officers' uniforms, did that happen prior to the takeover of Prijedor by the Serb authorities?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to what you've just read from the statement, it seems that this happened before the Serbs took over the police station and all the important institutions in the town. But I still say that this has faded from my memory.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: From April 30th, 1992, through May 22nd, 1992, sir, was there ever an attack on the village in which you lived in, Biscani? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no attack.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Were there any arrests during that interval period of April 30th through May 22nd, 1992, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that there were arrests, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And when, sir, and of whom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say exactly when, but I remember that whenever a police car appeared, they were looking for people who used to be policemen or who had some political posts, and these were the people who were arrested.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Did you, sir, at any time from April 30th, 1992, through May 22nd, 1992, ever assist in the preparation of a barricade or checkpoint on or around the village of Biscani where you resided?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not assist in the preparation of any sort of checkpoint. The only thing I did was that together with my father, without any weapons, I patrolled the area around our home to protect my mother and sister. That was all we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you know, sir, or are you familiar with where the checkpoint or barricade leading to your village, Biscani, was in April and May of 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that there was a checkpoint on the Ljubija Road just below Hambarine.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And do you know when that checkpoint, sir, was established or set up?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you know, sir, if that was a Muslim, a Serb, or a mixed checkpoint?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was manned by Muslims, because the population in the area was exclusively Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you know, sir, whether the Muslims who were controlling that checkpoint, whether they were armed or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never visited the checkpoint. I never saw it myself. I only heard that it existed.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Did you hear, sir, whether or not the men who were controlling the checkpoint or barricade were armed or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard that they were armed, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you know, sir, how long that checkpoint that you're referencing, how long it remained in existence after April of 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you know or did anyone tell you, sir, why a checkpoint was established on the outskirts of Hambarine?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you know or have you learned from any source, sir, who they were trying to keep out, if anyone, from entering the Brdo region, namely, Hambarine and Biscani, which required them to set up a checkpoint and/or barricade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Let's move, if we can, sir, to the actual Hambarine incident on May 22nd, 1992. You referenced yesterday on page 9, lines 15 through 18 approximately that you heard the news from men in a motorcycle or men in motorcycles. Do you remember that testimony?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether these men were actually people who were representative of the Territorial Defence of the Brdo region?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: These people -- I don't know whether they were members of the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you know, sir, if they were members of the local Crisis Staff of the Brdo region?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think they were. I think they were just ordinary people, that they were neither members of the Territorial Defence, nor...

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Nor what, sir? Nor the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: I assume they were members of neither the Crisis Staff nor the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: On or about May 22nd, 1992, sir, is it true that the Muslim population in the Brdo region actually maintained and had a Territorial Defence as well as a Crisis Staff established?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Did you, sir, ever become familiar with the individuals who were members of the Muslim Crisis Staff from the Brdo region in May of 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: These were people who were secretaries in the local community, the local commune, or who had some sort of post in the local commune.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And do you remember any of their names, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember because they were neighbours of mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And can you share with us some of the individuals who were members of the Crisis Staff in May of 1992 in the Brdo region?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't want to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I would ask the Court perhaps to assist us, and maybe go into private or closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Let's please go into private session and let us hear the comments of the representative of the OTP.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I would just object on relevance. What relevance are the names of the people who were on the Crisis Staff and justify their -- if they were victims, if they were killed, it certainly wouldn't justify that. I don't see any relevance to getting those names.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If I may reply, that objection actually is so far afield from what this process is all about. The OTP has called witnesses who have been in consistent denial about various issues that we believe are very well known and should have been stipulated to by the OTP, not as purposes of Defence and whether there was any justification for their death, but actually for veracity of witnesses. Here we have a gentleman that is willing to actually share with us, I hope, in closed and private session, who these individuals are, and it's our duty, I believe, respectfully to determine who were all the players at the relevant time period. We cannot get more relevant than the issue of May 1992. Which heard from many witnesses and I dare say that those witnesses that this individual will identify are the same witnesses that were before this Court. So how an objection on relevancy can ever be made much less sustained is beyond comprehension. Secondly, we believe that this issue with Crisis Staff has been enormously and egregiously overstated. Crisis Staff, as the OTP would like to attribute to our client was far different than the reality, Your Honour. And I think this witness can help assist us in to understanding why at times some individuals may have identified a Crisis Staff and certain members who were Serbian within that Crisis Staff. Each region may have had one. Each separate enclave may have had one. And we think it's very relevant and important in this case because it goes to issues not only of chain of command but superior responsibility because we're accused of both 7(1) and 7(3) in the revised fourth amended indictment as well as others issues relating to discriminatory intent as well as factors relating to deportation and authorisation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I didn't follow all the from that argument how the names are relevant. We have never denied that there were Territorial Defence units and Crisis Staffs in other parts of Prijedor Municipality. The accused in this case is charged not because they used the name "Crisis Staff" but because of what that body, that Crisis Staff of the Serbian Municipality did. I still don't see how the names of the particular individuals are relevant, and I submit it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: For the evaluation of evidence, it may be of assistance to know about the names, and therefore we regard this as relevant. But we have, of course, as regards the second part of your statement, who warned -- it's not for us to warn Defence but to tell the Defence that the notion of Crisis Staff itself has no meaning at all. We have to look into different Crisis Staffs. We had about 1.000 Crisis Staffs in Germany during the last month. So, please, refrain from making any comparison of this Crisis Staff and that Crisis Staff. And no doubt, that in such a situation, each part tries to defend him or herself. And therefore, I would ask to go in -- are we already in private session? If not, then we should go.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Confirmed.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Witness X, we're again in open session. And thank you. Just a couple questions for the period of April 6th or 7th when you came to Prijedor from Sarajevo up until May 22nd, 1992. Do you know, sir, whether the school continued to operate throughout that entire period up until the incident at Hambarine, May 22nd, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean elementary schools or secondary schools?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Either or both.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: Secondary schools did not operate, because no one had access to the town. That's across the bridge, because you had to cross the bridge on your way from the villages to the town there was a checkpoint, and no one went to school any more, not secondary school students.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: How about elementary school students, sir? Did they continue to go to school up until May of 1992 and towards the end of May 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember that, whether elementary schools continued to operate in certain local communes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Following the incident on May 22nd, 1992, at Hambarine that we have been discussing, you mentioned that there was an announcement made on Radio Prijedor. Within that announcement, can you tell me, sir, who made the announcement? Who was the individual or individuals who made the announcement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: Radio Prijedor announced this, and I can't say who the person was because I don't know. We listened to Radio Prijedor, and they announced that there was a request for Aziz Aliskovic and his group to surrender. Those were the people who had allegedly manned and secured the checkpoint.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I understand that, sir. But is it your testimony that you don't recall by whom this announcement was made?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Prijedor Crisis Staff, I don't know. The announcement came through Radio Prijedor which was under the Serbian authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I understand that, sir. I'm specifically asking you, and isn't it true that you don't know and you don't recall specifically that there was an announcement made by the Crisis Staff following the May 22nd incident at Hambarine over Radio Prijedor? Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean "Crisis Staff"? I can't seem to understand your question. Could you please simplify it a bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I'll try. And you made the same request of the OTP on page 10 yesterday in connection with this announcement, and we transformed it. It was an announcement, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And that announcement, sir, that you recall following the incident of May 22nd, 1992, at Hambarine, it was made by someone over the radio broadcast, and you heard that announcement. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Isn't it also true, sir, that you don't recall, as you sit here today under oath, that that announcement was made by the Crisis Staff, by the military, by the police, or by any other civil authorities? Correct? You just don't know who made that announcement; true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember. The announcement came through Radio Prijedor, but I can't remember who released the statement. And Radio Prijedor was Serb controlled because they had taken over all the media on the same day as the takeover of the town. Now, whether it was released by the police or the Crisis Staff, frankly, I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may, with respect to the interpretation, we believe the witness said he wasn't sure if it was the military police or Crisis Staff, but the transcription only reflects the answer as being police and/or Crisis Staff, on page 31, line 10 through 11, to the extent that it may be important.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please feel free to ask another time for clarification.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Witness X, just for clarification, as you sit here today under oath, you do not recall whether this announcement following the May 22nd, 1992, incident at Hambarine, whether it was issued by either the Crisis Staff, military police, or any other civil authorities. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember. I assume it was the Crisis Staff, but I can't offer you any specific argument.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: That's fine. Can you tell us, sir, at the very least what the contents of that announcement was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: The announcement said that Aziz Aliskovic and his group were to surrender. If they didn't surrender, the village would be shelled.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And the village specifically was Hambarine. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: From May 22nd, 1992, through July 20th, 1992, prior to the time that you were taken to Trnopolje, was the village in which you resided, Biscani, ever attacked in either May, June, or July 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were several attacks, artillery attacks, from the surrounding villages.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And sir, can you tell me when that was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember the 11th of July, 1992. That's the Serbian holiday of Petrovdan, and I remember they fired shells on that day all over Brdo, and they burned houses in Hambarine.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: My question, though, sir specifically is relating to your town, Biscani. Was that ever attacked in May, June, and July 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: The village of Biscani was also attacked that same night by artillery.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Other than that day, Petrovdan, any other days, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Can you list them for me?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember the dates, but I remember that within the same time span that Hambarine was taken, around the 20th of July, most of -- in the afternoon hours, there were attacks. There was shelling.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, and let me just move in the interests of time to another area. While you were at Trnopolje, from July 20th, 1992, through August 21st approximately, 1992, is it fair to state, sir, that there was no fence in Trnopolje camp while you were there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a fence in Trnopolje, but when delegations of international organisations arrived, the fence would be removed every time and then they would put it back up.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Help me with this, sir, on page 8, sorry, of your 19th May, 1998 statement, in the third paragraph you state as follows, which has ERN number 03004397, and again, sir, to refresh your recollection, this is the statement given to the federal office of criminal investigation.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: May I continue, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: It states there: "In Trnopolje, we were shut in an abandoned shop for the first night. Later we were only able to stay outside on the grass where we also slept. The camp was guarded. There was no fence, and there were generally so many Muslims in the camp that it was thoroughly overcrowded." Can you reconcile, sir, your statement to the federal criminal investigators on the 19th of May, 1998, and your testimony here today that there was a fence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't give you a precise answer, but I know that there was a wire fence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Sorry, I have to interrupt. It's totally misleading. It's not your fault. In the German version, it says: "There was a fence." It's translated: "There was no fence." Sorry to state this.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, we're just going by the English version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: The German version, page 7, paragraph 3. Second or -- third paragraph, sentence 3, it reads: "Es gas eimen Zaim," "There was a fence." I don't know how it's possible that this translation occurs.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I think Mr. Ostojic should be sanctioned for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, if we can just proceed if I may.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Before we proceed, because I see it's close to the half hour, I do have a confession to make in that from counsel's earlier questions, I was double-checking the disclosures. And there is a transcript of -- can we go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Yes, please, in private session. I hope this is settled, and you can rely, please, with some assistance of another German native speaker, you can --

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: We'll certainly accept the Court's reading on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please be seated. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. We can proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: We are in open session now, just for clarification.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Witness X. Thank you for your patience. We're trying to clarify some issues, and we appreciate to the extent that you can help us, that you do so. Obviously, as you have this morning, if you don't recall, simply tell us, and I'll be glad to move to another area or seek clarification by trying to either refresh your recollection or by other means available and permitted to us by the Court. Just so we can clarify the point on Trnopolje, and you heard obviously the Court's comments on that in the German version, we have only the English version that we are able to at least read. Since you were there, sir, from July 20th through August 21st, 1992, is it true, sir, that to the extent that there was a fence there that the fence did not encompass the entire Trnopolje camp as you've identified?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have already said that in the Trnopolje camp, there was a primary school, and there was a gym in the school. There was also an abandoned shop. The wire fence we are talking about was where there was grass, not all the way around because there was already a metal fence in front of the school, around the school and the gym, up to the road. However, behind the school where there was grass, that's where the wire fence was put up.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Can you to the best of your recollection describe that fence as well as its dimensions; namely, its height, length, and the type of fencing it was that was put up.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was barbed wire, and it was over 2 metres high. As for the length, I can't remember because I didn't really walk around the perimeter. I was only inside near the school and the gym.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Another question with respect to your detention at Trnopolje camp, it relates to the Red Cross. Do you remember whether or not the Serbian Red Cross was present at the Trnopolje camp during the time that you were there, July 20th through August 21st, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 20th of July, I arrived in Trnopolje and spent the night in the abandoned shop. And on the following morning, two women wearing Red Cross insignia turned up and registered all the inmates. After we were registered, we were allowed to go into the compound of the camp. That's where I saw the Red Cross.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Did you, sir, see the Red Cross at any time subsequent to that initial meeting on or about July 21st, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't because I didn't leave the compound. After that date, I never left the compound for a single moment. It was only people who had an identity card who could leave the compound. I didn't have one, so I could not go out looking for food the way other people did.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Help me with this statement that was translated, and again, I can't attest to the accuracy of the translation from the (redacted) that, from the interview. I should ask the Court to strike that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Unfortunately, it's already -- please, redact this word.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour, I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, it states on page 6 of this summary or translation of an interview that you gave to a third country on ERN number L0074938, in the lower portion starting with the word "Trnopolje" it's described as follows: "Trnopolje was a village, a kind of big village, where people worked before the war. They had their gardens that were left after they had been forced to go away -- go away from their houses, and so the soldiers decided to let us, who were in the camp, look for food and simply kind of loot, plunder, the houses, look for flour, blankets, and everything else we needed." With respect to that statement, sir, can you quantify for us the number of people that were permitted to go outside the Trnopolje camp or Detention Centre to look for food, clothing, blankets, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say. I can't say how many. I wasn't interested in that at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you know --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: People who needed to go went.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you know, sir, if this was a daily occurrence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the very beginning, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you again, if I may, with respect to the Red Cross that may have been there. During the time that the convoy was assembled on August 21st, 1992, when you left the Trnopolje camp, who was present during that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the 21st of August, you mean? Well, it was only uniformed persons who were present.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Tell me how many and to the extent that you know their names, list them for me, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can say how many there were, although I didn't count them. I saw a school friend of mine, Dragan Knezevic. I saw Branko Topala. I saw Dado. I don't know what his last name. He was a neighbour or a colleague or a relative of Dragan Knezevic. I don't know about the others.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: With respect to this convoy that assembled -- strike that. Sir, once you were at Mount Vlasic, you said that there were soldiers who a day or three days subsequent to that incident on August 21st, 1992, that they approached you when they found you. Is it fair to state, sir, that those soldiers did not beat or threaten you in any way?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. They treated me kindly.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And tell me, sir, what the ethnicity of those soldiers was.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: They didn't introduce themselves, but I assume they were of Serb ethnicity because they were wearing olive-grey uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, if I may just discuss with you the hospitalization on August 31st, 1992, when you were being treated for the injury that you sustained regrettably to your leg. Sir, in your statement, on page 7, of September 12th through the 13th, 1996, given to the ICTY, again, page 7, third full paragraph, you discuss that a Muslim doctor drained your leg by opening the scar. Can you tell me, sir, what the name of that Muslim doctor was.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't want to say the name of that man. I can't say for reasons of security because he probably played a key role in relation to my leg, and he would -- or rather, had he not played that role, the consequences would have been drastic. When I was released allegedly, I talked to that doctor, and he said they were going to amputate my leg above the knee, and then send me to the military medical academy in Belgrade to have my leg amputated from the hip.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: To the best of your recollection, sir, was this Muslim doctor actually the director of this medical clinic in which you sought treatment in Banja Luka on the 31st of August, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't ask to be treated. It just happened that way due to circumstances. I don't know what the doctor's post in the hospital was. I wasn't allowed to talk to the doctors directly in the hospital because every time he appeared, he was escorted by a guard. And the guard was always standing close to us, so we just had eye contact, but we didn't speak.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Help me understand how was it this conversation that was relayed to you with respect to your amputation either being below the knee, above the knee, or up through and to your hip. When did this occur if you didn't speak to the doctor?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I was released from hospital, and when I had gained a little strength and was able to talk to people, it was then that he told me, and he told me that the worst was over. That was in November.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Of 1992. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, 1992, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would ask that we go into private session so that we could obtain the name of the doctor, and it goes I think to a threshold issue that the OTP is trying to establish, or one of their purported threshold issues, namely that there was a dismissal and discharge of all Muslim intellectuals and professionals, and so I think it's necessary at least to make that nexus.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please help me understanding, if it's undisputed that there was a Muslim doctor, what's the relevance of the name?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: We think that we can establish, Your Honour, that this individual was at all times the director and the person who was the head of the clinic in Banja Luka during the entire period. We hope by obtaining this name that we can get into contact with the physician so that he can clarify, if not rebut the broad statements by the Prosecutor that all Muslims who were educated or professionals were dismissed. And we are contending that that is not accurate respectfully.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think that the little relevance that it has would be outweighed by misuse of time and the possible danger to someone. Again, this is taking place in Banja Luka, not in Prijedor. So its relevance to the particular case of Dr. Stakic is very, very limited. And if this is admitted, one witness -- one name of one doctor who remained working in Banja Luka, then, of course, all of our evidence regarding all of the doctors in Banja Luka university, administrators, et cetera, would then become relevant to rebut the fact that one Muslim was allowed to continue working. And I think overall, that would not be relevant and useful use of our time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: The request of the Defence is dismissed.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Witness X, with respect to the individual that you identified yesterday in your transcript by the name of Edin Mrkalj, on page 44 and 45 of the transcript, and again, we are in open session, sir, so can you please identify for me what this individual's father's name is.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mrkalj.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me, sir, what the fate of this individual was, because I don't think we received it when you were discussing it on pages 44 and 45 of yesterday's transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Could the question just be clarified, are we talking about the father or son in the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The son, Edin Mrkalj.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: What happened to him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, he ended up in camp after turning in his weapons and uniform, he ended up in camp. I assume it was in Omarska.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And what happened to him after that, sir? Do you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you know, sir, if he's alive or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: He's alive.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Is this an individual who was a police officer at one time in that municipality? Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I just have to ask you this question because it was unclear from other information that I received. Had you ever, sir, seen the police van that was used in the Prijedor Municipality in 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please speak into the microphone. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I saw it in Trnopolje.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: With respect to this police van, sir, can you tell me how many people can fit in the front seat?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say. I didn't dare approach it. There was nothing else for me to do there.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Let me just a couple more questions with respect to the convoy of August 21st, 1992. With respect to this August 21st, 1992, convoy, I'm going to read from -- again, I apologise if the translation is not correct. On page 9 of your 19th of May, 1998, statement, on the second or the first full paragraph, ERN number 03004398: "I can only remember that shortly before the 21st of August, 1992, he threatened that I would leave the camp with this convoy. In hindsight, I believe that he not do this in order to rescue me. Rather he knew very well that the men of this convoy of 21st August would be shot, because this convoy was the last opportunity to get prisoners out of the camp before they were registered by the International Red Cross. There was indeed an official registration by the Red Cross on 24 August of 1992." With respect to that, sir, if you left with the convoy on the 21st of August, 1992, how do you know that the International Red Cross was present and actually registered detainees at the Trnopolje camp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the 21st of August, some neighbours of mine and some members of my family stayed behind in the camp. Fortunately, they had not been put on the convoy. And I had an opportunity to talk to them, so I obtained this information from my relatives and neighbours who stayed behind in the camp. After the 21st of August, that was a Friday, on the following Monday, the Red Cross turned up and registered all the prisoners left in the Trnopolje camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: So is it fair to say this was a different registration than the one you experienced and testified that occurred when you were initially brought to Trnopolje on July 20th and 21st, 1992. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. The first registration that was carried out was carried out only by the local authorities. It was not by an international organisation.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Other than the one announcement that you heard over Radio Prijedor on May 22nd, 1992, did you hear any other announcements or can you recall any other announcements over Radio Prijedor following May 22nd, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: The announcement about the turning in of weapons and military equipment.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you recall, sir, a couple days after the incident in Hambarine there was a military announcement over Radio Prijedor which asked that the checkpoints in Jakupovici be moved back 100 metres from the main road so that the military convoy can pass through? Do you recall hearing that over the Radio Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: Jakupovici, that's something quite different. That's not in the area I come from. And that's a completely different piece of information.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: But sir, do you remember hearing that announcement over Prijedor radio on or about May 24th, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you recall, sir, the time May 24th, 1992, or do you have any information as to whether or not Muslims at a checkpoint in Jakupovici attacked a military convoy that was passing through the Banja Luka and Prijedor Road?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had different information that the checkpoint in Jakupovici had been attacked by Serbian soldiers or policemen. That's the information I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: That information that you have, sir, did not come from Radio Prijedor, right? It came from another source presumably?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you know, we were free to talk and look at what was happening around us.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Help me with this, sir: On May 30th, 1992, do you have information with respect to any attack on the actual city of Prijedor by Muslims or Muslim citizens?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had no information about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Is it fair to state, sir, that this is the first time you're hearing that there was an attack by Muslims citizens on the actual town of Prijedor on May 30th, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard it only in the morning. When dawn broke, we heard shooting. We were close to Prijedor, and we could hear the shooting, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Did you know or did you learn, sir, who was the participants on the Muslim citizens side who attacked the town of Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Just one more I think area I need to cover with you, sir. Thank you for your patience. Can you tell me who Zoran Karlica is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: Zoran Karlica, what I heard is that he was a person with a military rank. How should I put this? He was a senior officer, a senior military officer, because the day when the ethnic cleansing took place, all the people who took part in it were wearing insignia "Zoran Karlica."

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, isn't it true, at least according to your statement of the 19th of May, 1998, that Zoran Karlica had been one of the most senior military leaders from the barracks, he was killed shortly before the ethnic cleansing in May of 1992"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: The most senior, I'm not sure that this is what I stated. He was one of the senior officers of the army. On that day, the day of the cleansing, that was what I heard from the other soldiers who wore the insignia with the name "Zoran Karlica." They told me they wanted revenge because apparently he had been killed during the attack on Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, is it true, sir, do you agree with me that any action that may have been taken against the Muslims in Biscani occurred after your arrest on the 20th of July, 1992? Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: It happened on that very day, the 20th, the day I was arrested, and also after that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: But at no time prior to July 20th, 1992. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: It's not correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, I fail to understand your question because I've told you what had been happening up to that point, the 20th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Fair enough. Let me reconcile it. On page 6 of your 19th May, 1998, statement, you state, the last sentence of that first paragraph: "The Serbs first took action against the Muslims in Biscani after my arrest on 20th July, 1992." Is that true and accurate?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not defined, took measures, I mean. There's no clarification there in this quote, right, is there? What I know, the 20th of July, that's when the ethnic cleansing took place.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Witness X. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness X, may I please ask you some additional questions, just for completeness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Witness, are you married? Do you have a child?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am married, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And the age of your child?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have two children. One is 6, and the other 2 years old.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. What about your political activity at that time, in 1992? Before 1992, have you ever been a member of a political party?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: While I was in my regular military service for the JNA, the Yugoslav People's Army, I became a member of the league of communists.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: In your statement of May 1998, once again, mistake, you can see on the English version it's always stated May 1999, no doubt it was May 1998. You emphasise "passive member of the League of Communists of Yugoslavia." Is that correct, "passive member," and what's the meaning of "passive member"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: While I was the -- in the JNA, during my regular military service, due to my merits there, my good work, I was asked whether I would like to join the League of Communists of Yugoslavia, and I said yes. However, after my military service, I took no active part in the party's work. I only had my membership document. It was the same with my father. He was also a member of the League of Communists of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. I think it's easy to understand this at that time natural link between work and being member of the League of Communists. Have you ever been a member of the SDA?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never. Nor did I ever wish to join the SDA.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Why?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: I simply had no wish to become a member of any of those nationalist parties. I grew up and went to school with people who belonged to all the different ethnic groups, Serbs, Croats, Muslims, and that's the way I was raised. I was not taking into account the people's ethnic background.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Just one remaining question: I didn't really understand the meaning of the word yesterday when you mentioned that a person was armed with a CZ-99 firearm and a scorpio. Could you please explain what a scorpio is.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's an automatic pistol.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: So it was in addition to this other CZ-99?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I merely assumed that that was the name of the pistol, and the person who carried the pistol was saying these words.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you for this clarification. One other minor issue: You spoke several times about currencies yesterday. What was the ordinary currency you used at that time in 1992 in your country?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 1992, I can't say. 1999, that was a long time after the war. Perhaps you meant to refer to a different year.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I just wanted to refer to 1992, what was the ordinary currency to -- probably it may assist that yesterday you mentioned that there was a different currency introduced, and I want to invite you to comment a little bit on this alleged introduction of a different currency. You spoke about Serbian bank notes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember there used to be bank notes which only existed in Serb-held territory during the war in 1992. But I can't remember exactly whether the name of that currency was dinars or what the name was. But you could use -- you could only use that currency, that particular currency, in Serb-held territory and territory under the Serbian authorities.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And what was the currency you had to use after April 1992, say, in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: That same currency.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And the same was true in Trnopolje?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: On yesterday's transcript, page 51, line 8, you stated: "And here I could hear the person saying `here we exchange dead Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. for the dead and living for the living.'" The question was which person said that. Your answer was: "The same person that I believe is called Dragan Mrdja." Would you be able to recognise this Dragan Mrdja, and did you know Mr. Mrdja beforehand?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could try to identify him, although that was ten years ago. Memories fade. But what I noticed in that moment, I still have an image in my head of that, so I would be willing to give it a try, but I can't guarantee that I would be able to recognise the person. But I can try at least.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Had you met this person beforehand? Sometimes you mentioned "this person, this was my teacher in this or that school, another person I met at this or that occasion beforehand. Did you meet Mr. Dragan Mrdja beforehand on another occasion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember, at least I don't have a striking memory. The only image I still have of him that is relatively clear is the one I kept after the execution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: But you still have this image before you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, well, I do remember something.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Would you please be so kind and tell us if there is something special you remember about this person.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: Anything in particular. Well, maybe the eyebrows, wide, not that much but perhaps above average.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Let's leave it with this for the moment.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: Or perhaps the round shape of his head.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Probably we have to come back to this later. Let me finally ask: Did you ever before 1992 or in 1992 hear directly or via other persons the name of Dr. Stakic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: If you personally think back, and far away from all legal aspects, what do you believe, who is responsible for that what happened to you and for that what you had to tell us yesterday?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't specify. I can't point to an individual, but the orders had to come from somewhere, from someplace. And then perhaps someone had to pass on these orders, someone had to give the orders and someone else had to carry them out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Didn't you have any insight in the hierarchy of the police forces in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: The hierarchy, you mean, anarchy?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I wanted to stay neutral and speak about hierarchy. And at that time, when you came back to Prijedor following that on perusal what you said earlier, especially in 1998, you found the 6th of April the police forces in a relatively coordinated shape. You mentioned that only one month later, this person - unfortunately I forgot the name - was exchanged. Is that true, that when you came back, you were ordered to come back by Mr. Balic? This was already quoted to the transcript by the Defence counsel. You met that person you named as chief of police, Fikret Kadiric, and then you mentioned the 1st of May, 1992, police station in Prijedor was taken over by Serbs and Mr. Kadiric was dismissed. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And who took over, to the best of your recollection, the post of Mr. Kadiric?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember who did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Mr. Kadiric was a Muslim. Right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I have no further questions in the moment. Judge Fassi Fihri? Judge Vassylenko.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Witness X, in your statement made in 1996, you reported about three episodes of killings of Muslims by Serbs. Can you tell us how many persons were killed during these killings, and how these persons, these victims, were selected?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say exactly how many people were killed. First, they killed the people who held official appointments and positions, intellectuals. And then later, whether it was a random selection or whether it depended on the feelings of those who had arrived there to kill people or something like that, I don't know. But I can't say with precision how many people were killed. However, many people were killed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Thank you. I have no more questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Any additional questions emanating from the line of questions from the Judges?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, not directly emanating from the line of questions, but I would just ask leave of the Court to ask just one follow-up question which relates to a name that the individual gave -- the witness gave yesterday during the direct examination in open session, just the transcript doesn't seem to reflect the first name of the individual. And it appears on page 66, line 25. It's my recollection that he did give the name, the first name as well as the surname, just that it doesn't appear in the daily copy that we were given yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Yes. There's this famous symbol for leaving out a name. May I ask the registry, on the official version, can we see the full name of this person? Hopefully we can facilitate and just ask you, Witness X, yesterday you mentioned a Mr. Kurstic. What is the first name of this person, Kurstic?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I think it's Kustric, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I read --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's Kustric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: What's the first name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: Alija.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Alija Kustric. Any further questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Just one matter to clear up.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: When you talked about the chief of police, I believe you said Fikret Kadiric, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: Chief of police, yes, I mentioned him.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: When you say chief of police, do you mean the chief of police for the opstina of Prijedor or do you mean the chief of police in the town of Prijedor, the head of the police in the town?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: Chief of the police station in Prijedor, and all the rest, the local ones were probably loyal to that police station.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Did you know Mr. Talundzic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS X [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: The only other matter I wanted to raise, Your Honour, is to just to ask to go into private session and just for our records to have the witness in private session state his name so we have Witness X's name official.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Yes, please let's go in private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Wasn't it an idea by the OTP, did the OTP already try to confront this witness during his stay here in The Hague with Mr. Mrdja?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. I'm a little hesitant to address it without Mr. Dimitrijevic, counsel for Mr. Mrdja. But I don't think there's any harm. We plan -- I spoke to him on the telephone yesterday, and I haven't directly talked to him because he's coming Wednesday next week. But we would be setting up an identification procedure, or attempting to, with this and at least one other witness in the future since that case has been put off quite indefinitely, and because of various problems, it was not --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Don't be so pessimistic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Does the Defence see any disadvantage by the nonconfrontation with Mr. Mrdja, especially as regards the personal responsibility for that what happened? Because if so, we have to arrange the necessary.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Unfortunately, Your Honour, we haven't had a chance to consult with Dr. Stakic, nor with Mr. Lukic specifically on this issue. But when you asked the question of disadvantage, we do believe that we are being disadvantaged by the OTP calling this witness, and then providing us with a translated version of a videocassette tape that they certainly have in their possession that was never given to us. And we think from that, as well as the additional eight statements this witness has, whether or not the OTP has it, I think it's incumbent upon them to set out and give us copies of all of those statements. And perhaps then once we obtain the totality of those statements we can compare it to whether or not this witness believes Mr. Mrdja individually Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. under 7(1) or under 7(3), had any exposure or culpability with respect to the crimes at Mount Vlasic. Until we get that, it's very difficult to say. Yes, I think this witness would be helpful and we think from some of the statements it clearly shows that the convoy was taken on a detour from yesterday's direct examination, that this was something that happened as an immediate response of some sort. Even though there were some conclusory remarks made by the witness and by the OTP, we dispute that, and hope to present evidence to the contrary. Since we don't have all the documents necessary to make an informed decision, we can only speculate and ask the Court that we be given a reservation so that we can inquire further only once we've obtained those documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: It's not difficult to foresee your reaction; therefore, I'm really hesitant. What is the estimated time this witness will stay in The Hague, Witness X?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: VWU I'm sure would take the witness, arrange for his travel back either tonight or tomorrow, once he's completed his stay here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I really want to avoid a situation that with some merits, the Defence can come with the issue that they are not really prepared because they didn't have access to all these other documents, and especially the video. How long would it take you to prepare these documents and grant it, both to the Defence and the Bench?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: All of the documents that -- statements of the witness I believe are now disclosed. The transcript of the video we do have a copy of the videotape if counsel wanted it, although it's in a language that I believe counsel does not understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: It's -- we are in open session? It's -- the language from a Nordic state?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please feel free to provide the Bench with some knowledge of this language with a copy of this video. And probably we can find out from our point of view if it's necessary. And the second point, no doubt, is whether, and therefore, I made reference yesterday to the question whether it's your intention to call Mr. Mrdja and try to find out by confrontation whether or not this witness, Witness X, is able to recognise Mr. Mrdja. And then, of course, we have all -- it's not only a factual problem, as you've already indicated, it's a problem of the legal responsibility; and therefore, one might have the obligation at least to try whether or not Mr. Mrdja is prepared to give testimony or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I realise I'm not --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: So we have three issues: Video, confrontation, attempt to hear the testimony of Mr. Mrdja.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: The video, we can provide to the Chamber, as a courtesy, and to counsel, if they would like it. The confrontation or any attempt to call Mr. Mrdja, no, we don't intend to do that. In my jurisdiction, that actually would be a sanctionable offence by an attorney to -- when I know that the attorney representing Mr. Mrdja has indicated to me he does not want me to contact his client, for me to bring his client or to make direct contact with his client.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: So it could be for the Chamber to call this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Correct. And as for the identification of Mr. Mrdja, although it's certainly a very relevant to the case against Mr. Mrdja, and this witness forms a very small part of that identification evidence.
