I don't want to go into the other evidence we have in that case, but the identification of that individual I don't think is relevant -- of much relevance to this particular case. The witness has been clear that these police officers were from Prijedor that was escorting the convoy. Whether he can recognise one particular individual or not, name that individual, I don't think is as relevant as the issue in the Stakic is that these were members of the police from Prijedor and members of this special police unit Prijedor police.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: May I hear the comments of the Defence in order that we have a sound basis for the decision whether or not to call Mr. Mrdja ex officio.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, the Defence, Your Honour, is still puzzled as to the OTP's position in connection with Mount Vlasic and Mr. Mrdja. If they are contending that there is any responsibility for the crimes that are alleged to have happen on or about August 21st, 1992, under the superior command decisional authority that's before us, then they have to establish a nexus. If counsel can stand here before us and tell us that they have additional information on Mr. Mrdja that he does not think it relevant for this case I can't understand how that can at all be the case. If Mr. Mrdja and the Mount Vlasic issue is directly related to the Prijedor Municipality and Dr. Stakic, then all the evidence they have in connection with Mr. Mrdja should and is relevant relating to Dr. Stakic. But first, counsel not only being a representative of the OTP but also being one of the attorneys who is in charge and directly responsible for the prosecution of Mr. Mrdja could enlighten us and tell the Court whether or not the indictment against Mr. Mrdja is both 7(1) and 7(3). In that vein, if they are seeking from Mr. Mrdja that he is only individually responsible, it would be helpful to us. It would be helpful for the Court to understand that. We don't know, and did not investigate the theory that the OTP may have against Mr. Mrdja. This is a new development in this case. We think that we should be given all the documents relating to that if they truly believe there was even a remote possibility that there was an order given to take a couple or several convoys from the Prijedor Municipality all the way through Banja Luka and the Travnik area and execute individuals. They should put forth that evidence as opposed to just giving a round about way of telling us there was an individual who was in this specific police unit without listing directly what the nexus or link is to the municipality of Prijedor and possibly the leadership there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Would you personally have any objections against calling ex officio Mr. Mrdja as a witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I personally, Judge, I can tell the Court respectfully, most respectfully, that I do have an objection to it because I think that the rules specifically state the OTP has the burden of proof. And quite frankly, maybe it's my jurisdiction that we come from, but the OTP, if they make a tactical or strategic decision and fail to fulfill the requirements, that's a responsibility that they are going to have to carry with them. Again, the Court can do and obviously we'll accept whatever the Court wishes to do on this issue. But personally I do have an objection to it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. The OTP?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I just wanted to invite Mr. Ostojic to stop on his way out and pick up the indictment of Mr. Mrdja if he want to know the basis of the charges. They are 7(1). It's a public indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: The Trial Chamber has to find out, and the parties will see tomorrow what will happen. They can't say they are surprised. My only concern is could it be necessary that we have to recall Witness X tomorrow on the basis of the not-read documents, the not-seen videos, and for this purpose ask the responsible unit of this Tribunal to ask Witness X to stay here one day longer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I know that the witness specifically told me he wants to leave as soon as possible because of a work problem, both for he and his spouse when he's gone. As I understand it, they were -- one was working day and one was working night. And when he's gone, she cannot work because there's no child care and he is obviously not working. That's my understanding in speaking to him. As for the documents, the 13 and a half page double-spaced transcript was provided today. I think counsel has had a chance to read there's nothing else other than the watching the videotape where the witness is going to say what's in the transcript. If that's necessary, the witness, we can hold the witness for that purpose.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, respectfully, we don't or would not like to delay Witness X from going back to his family. But our objection is really that these documents should have been provided to us earlier. We're going to continue to object to that, and we're going to continue to present it before the Court because it happens not only on an isolated occasion, but it seems that it happens unfortunately more often than not. So we will not ask this witness questions in connection with this videotape, but we think it's necessary under the rules in this Tribunal that the Defence be provided a complete list of all these documents and all statements that they have in their possession, not at the eve of their testimony, or in the middle of their testimony or during the completion of the cross-examination. So we do object to that. We do not object to this witness going home as soon as possible with his wife and children and to attend to his personal needs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: So I can understand that on the basis of those documents given to you until now, and knowing that on the video you can't see anything more than that what you can see on this 13 and a half pages translated in a draft translation into English, there is no basis for you for additional questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Not at this time, Your Honour, with the exception of having an OTP witness who previously testified in other cases, Hanne Sofie Greve, a former judge doing the interrogating or the questioning purportedly, but I'll reserve those comments for either a Status Conference or at a later time. Correct, with respect to this witness and the information that's translated, subject to being translated correctly, we would have no further questions of this witness based on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: On the basis of the statements of the parties, we don't see any obstacles for Witness X to leave as soon as possible The Hague. But we'll leave it open, at least to try to hear Mr. Mrdja at the one or other point. Now it's not that urgent. The plan for tomorrow will be?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Witness Number 2 will be testifying tomorrow. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And for what period of time estimated?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Mr. Waidyaratne will be handling the witness, but I think our initial estimate was a day and a half.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. And to come back to that what was just recently discussed, we have all the statements and all exhibits provided for this witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I'll have Mr. Waidyaratne doublecheck that. And I certainly agree with counsel that it's our obligation to provide that. On this particular videotape, I take responsibility. But I think we missed it on the initial check because a pseudonym was used for the witness rather than the witness's name. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. Probably I'm wrong, but is it correct, Madam Registrar, that the famous list number 6 we received immediately before court recess with numerous 65 ter documents, these documents were not yet admitted into evidence? It starts probably, Ms. Karper, can help us out. For example, 65 ter 286, that's the first one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
